pages.lead: First, we get dressed and put on our backpack.
pages.body: Then we go to school with our family.

pages.lead: We ride the bus or walk to school.
pages.body: We stay close to our grown-up.

pages.lead: We say goodbye to our family.
pages.body: They will come back to pick us up.

pages.lead: We say hello to our teacher.
pages.body: Our teacher is happy to see us.

pages.lead: We find our seat in the classroom.
pages.body: We listen and learn new things.

pages.lead: At the end of the day, we go home.
pages.body: We can tell our family about our day.

pages.lead: First, we know we need the toilet.
pages.body: We can tell a trusted adult and go to the bathroom.

pages.lead: We pull down our pants and sit on the toilet.
pages.body: We can take our time. That is okay.

pages.lead: When we are done, we use toilet paper.
pages.body: We wipe from front to back.

pages.lead: We flush the toilet.
pages.body: It might be loud, and that is okay.

pages.lead: We pull up our pants.
pages.body: We check that our clothes are on right.

pages.lead: We wash our hands with soap and water.
pages.body: We scrub while we sing a little song.

pages.lead: We dry our hands with a towel.
pages.body: Now our hands are clean.

pages.lead: We did it!
pages.body: Going to the toilet is part of every day.

pages.lead: First, we go to the doctor.
pages.body: The doctor will check how we are feeling and help us stay healthy.

pages.lead: The doctor says hello.
pages.body: We can say hello back or wave.

pages.lead: The doctor listens to our heart.
pages.body: The stethoscope may feel cold. That is okay.

pages.lead: The doctor looks in our ears and mouth.
pages.body: We can open wide and say 'ahh'.

pages.lead: We can tell the doctor how we feel.
pages.body: It is okay to ask questions.

pages.lead: When we are done, we say thank you.
pages.body: Going to the doctor helps us stay well.

pages.lead: First, we get our toothbrush.
pages.body: Then we put toothpaste on it and brush our teeth.

pages.lead: We squeeze a little toothpaste.
pages.body: A tiny bit, like a pea, is just right.

pages.lead: We brush our front teeth and back teeth.
pages.body: Round and round, up and down.

pages.lead: We brush for two minutes.
pages.body: We can count or sing a song.

pages.lead: We spit out the toothpaste.
pages.body: Then we rinse our toothbrush.

pages.lead: Our teeth are clean and shiny!
pages.body: We brush in the morning and at night.

pages.lead: First, we sit at the table.
pages.body: Then we choose what we want and tell the person.

pages.lead: We look at the menu.
pages.body: We can point to pictures of food we like.

pages.lead: We wait for our food.
pages.body: Waiting can be hard. We can draw or talk quietly.

pages.lead: We eat our food with our family.
pages.body: We use our inside voice.

pages.lead: We say please and thank you.
pages.body: Good manners are kind.

pages.lead: When we are finished, we go home.
pages.body: Eating out can be fun.

pages.lead: First, we arrive at the airport.
pages.body: Then we check in and go through security.

pages.lead: We show our tickets and give our big bags.
pages.body: Our bags will meet us later.

pages.lead: We go through security.
pages.body: We put our things in a tray. The staff help keep us safe.

pages.lead: We wait at the gate.
pages.body: We can look at the planes through the window.

pages.lead: We get on the plane and find our seat.
pages.body: We buckle our seatbelt.

pages.lead: The plane goes up into the sky.
pages.body: Our ears may feel funny. We can swallow or yawn.

pages.lead: We land and ride to where we are going.
pages.body: We made it to our trip!

pages.lead: First, we wait for our turn.
pages.body: Then we can play together and be kind.

pages.lead: We go down the slide one at a time.
pages.body: We wait until the slide is clear.

pages.lead: We can ask a friend to play.
pages.body: We can say, 'Do you want to play with me?'

pages.lead: We take turns on the swings.
pages.body: Everyone gets a turn.

pages.lead: If someone gets hurt, we can help.
pages.body: We can find a trusted adult.

pages.lead: When it is time to go, we say goodbye.
pages.body: We can come back another day.

pages.lead: Sharing is kind.
pages.body: We can take turns and share our toys with friends.

pages.lead: We can ask, 'Can I have a turn?'
pages.body: Then we wait for our friend to answer.

pages.lead: We can give a toy to a friend.
pages.body: Our friend feels happy.

pages.lead: Sharing makes playing more fun.
pages.body: We can play together.

pages.lead: Sometimes we have to wait.
pages.body: We can play with something else while we wait.

pages.lead: We feel proud when we share.
pages.body: Sharing is being a good friend.

pages.lead: If we need help, we can ask a trusted adult.
pages.body: It is okay to ask for help.

pages.lead: Trusted adults are people like our family and teachers.
pages.body: They want to help us.

pages.lead: We can raise our hand or say, 'Help, please.'
pages.body: We use a calm voice.

pages.lead: We tell them what we need.
pages.body: We can use words, pictures, or point.

pages.lead: The adult listens and helps us.
pages.body: We say thank you.

pages.lead: Asking for help is brave.
pages.body: Everyone needs help sometimes.

pages.lead: We give people space.
pages.body: We do not stand too close to others.

pages.lead: An arm's length is a good space.
pages.body: We can stretch out our arm to check.

pages.lead: We ask before we hug.
pages.body: We can say, 'Can I have a hug?'

pages.lead: If someone says no, that is okay.
pages.body: We can wave or give a high five instead.

pages.lead: Other people give us space too.
pages.body: We can say, 'Please give me some space.'

pages.lead: Giving space helps everyone feel comfortable.
pages.body: Space is a way to be kind.

pages.lead: It is okay to say 'No, thank you.'
pages.body: We can say no if we don't want something.

pages.lead: We can use a kind voice.
pages.body: We can shake our head or say, 'No, thank you.'

pages.lead: Other people can say no to us too.
pages.body: We listen and say okay.

pages.lead: If we feel unsafe, we can say 'No!' loudly.
pages.body: Then we tell a trusted adult.

pages.lead: Our body belongs to us.
pages.body: We can say no to touches we do not want.

pages.lead: Saying no is okay.
pages.body: We can be kind and still say no.

pages.lead: We stay with our trusted adults.
pages.body: We follow safety rules like looking both ways before we cross.

pages.lead: We hold hands near busy roads.
pages.body: We stay on the sidewalk.

pages.lead: We wait for the green light.
pages.body: Green means walk. Red means stop.

pages.lead: If we get lost, we stay where we are.
pages.body: We can ask a helper, like a police officer or a shop worker.

pages.lead: We know our grown-up's name.
pages.body: This helps people find them.

pages.lead: Staying safe keeps us happy and healthy.
pages.body: We can always ask for help.
